mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome. I’m so glad you’re joining me for this journey—one that takes us through loss, hope, and the unexpected ways grace can show up right when we need it most. Imagine a place where heartbreak and despair aren’t the end of the story, but the very ground where something beautiful can take root. That’s exactly what we’ll explore together as we step into the world of A Love Story How God Pursued Me and Found Me: An Impossibly True Story—a deeply personal account penned by Samantha Ryan Chandler. Here, the lines between doubt and faith get blurry. You’ll see how the ache of abandonment, and that longing to truly belong, can be met with a quiet, persistent love—a love that never gives up, even when everything feels lost. As we move through this story, you’ll notice how moments of vulnerability open the door to resilience. The threads of struggle and spiritual awakening are woven tightly together, showing how healing can grow out of even the deepest wounds. What if the presence of God isn’t some distant idea, but a close companion, walking with you through every challenge? Together, we’ll discover how the hardest moments can become the starting point for restoration, and how trust—sometimes shaky at first—can lead to a faith that transforms. So, as we set out on this adventure, get ready to uncover a love that finds us right where we are, no matter how impossible things might seem. Let’s dive in, side by side, and see what hope and redemption really look like when the story is our own.

Chapter 1: Searching for Meaning in a World That Feels Empty
You know, there’s a certain kind of ache that settles in when life just doesn’t seem to add up. It’s that emptiness that lingers, even when everything on the outside looks perfectly fine. Maybe you’ve felt it—a quiet sense of being out of place, like there’s something essential missing but you can’t quite put your finger on it. That’s really where our story begins. Not with some dramatic crisis, but with a slow, persistent realization: the world keeps promising happiness and fulfillment, but somehow, it always falls short.
Growing up, the world can feel a bit like a puzzle with a few missing pieces. Sure, there are moments of laughter, family get-togethers, the comfort of everyday routines. But underneath it all, there’s this subtle restlessness that just won’t go away. When you’re young, there’s such a longing to belong, to be seen and truly loved for who you are. Sometimes, that longing gets met with disappointment—relationships don’t last, friendships fade, and you wind up feeling misunderstood.
Even with all that, there’s still this quiet hope inside, whispering that maybe—just maybe—something more is out there. Some folks try to fill that void with achievements, chasing after good grades, sports trophies, or the approval of others. Others dive into distractions: music, movies, or the endless scroll through social media, hoping to drown out that nagging sense of incompleteness. But, no matter how much you achieve or how many distractions you pile on, that emptiness just sticks around.
For one young woman, this search for meaning became the defining thread of her early life. She grew up in a home where faith was more like background noise than a guiding force. Church was something you endured, not something you embraced, and prayers felt more like empty words than anything real. The idea of a loving God? It just seemed distant, almost irrelevant to the ups and downs of daily life.
As the years rolled by, the gap between what life was and what it could be just kept getting wider. Of course, there were moments of joy—family vacations, inside jokes with siblings, the thrill of new experiences. But those moments were fleeting, always chased away by that old, familiar ache. It was easy to start believing that maybe this was it: a life spent going through the motions, always hoping for something better but never really finding it.
High school only made things more intense. The pressure to fit in was overwhelming—always balancing between wanting to be accepted and trying to stay true to yourself. Sometimes, it just felt easier to blend in, to hide your doubts and fears behind a mask of confidence. But even in a crowded hallway or a noisy cafeteria, loneliness could sneak in. It wasn’t about being physically alone—it was about feeling unseen.
During those years, questions about purpose and identity got louder. What’s the point of all this? Is there a reason behind the pain and confusion? Most people around her seemed happy to ignore those questions, focusing on the next big event or the latest trend. But for her, those questions just wouldn’t go away.
And then, in the middle of all that searching, little hints of something greater started to show up. Sometimes it was a quiet moment of peace right in the middle of chaos. Other times, it felt like someone was watching over her, even when things were falling apart. Easy to dismiss these moments as coincidence, but they planted tiny seeds of curiosity. Could there be a purpose behind all this pain? Was someone reaching out, even when she wasn’t looking?
Looking back, it’s pretty clear that the journey toward faith rarely starts with certainty. More often, it begins with longing—a deep desire for meaning, for love, for something real. It’s a journey filled with questions and doubts, and the slow realization that the answers the world offers just aren’t enough.
So if you’ve ever felt lost or unseen, you’re not alone. This is where the story truly begins: in that quiet ache for something more.

Chapter Two: Hitting Rock Bottom and Facing Brokenness
There comes a moment in life when the weight of disappointment and pain just feels too heavy to bear. Sometimes it creeps in slowly, unraveling bit by bit. Other times, it hits like a sudden collapse. No matter how it happens, reaching rock bottom is scary—but oddly, it also brings a certain clarity.
All the illusions we've held onto get stripped away, and we're left facing the truth: things aren’t okay, and pretending just isn't working anymore.
When you’re stepping into adulthood, that pressure to have it all together only grows. Maybe you’re juggling college, a new job, or relationships. There’s so much excitement, but right alongside it comes anxiety and a bunch of new chances to fall short.
I want to share the story of one young woman making that leap into independence. For her, the freedom to chart her own course was thrilling, but it also meant she had to deal with the consequences of her own choices—good or bad.
At first, it was easy for her to believe that success would equal happiness. Getting good grades, chasing a promising career, keeping a packed social calendar—those all seemed like the golden ticket to fulfillment. But underneath, old hurts never really left. There was the sting of rejection, the fear of not measuring up, and the shame that clings from past mistakes—always lurking just out of sight.
As life’s demands piled up, so did the feeling of overwhelm. Some mornings, even getting out of bed felt impossible. The future looked like a dark tunnel, with no light ahead. In those moments, it was tempting to find ways to numb the pain. Some people reach for unhealthy relationships, hoping someone else can fill the emptiness. Others try to escape through substances, endless distractions, or burying themselves in work. But none of it really works. Instead, these things just deepen the isolation and despair.
For her, the breaking point didn’t come with a big blow-up. It was more of a quiet realization—she just couldn’t put herself back together. The old strategies like denial, distraction, or stubborn self-reliance? They stopped working. Instead of relief, they left her feeling even more alone. The mask of having it all together started to slip, and her real fear and brokenness began to show.
Yet, in the midst of all that darkness, something new started to grow. It wasn’t just a wish for happiness anymore—it was a desperate need for rescue. The idea of God, which once seemed distant or irrelevant, began to mean something different. Could it be possible that someone actually cared enough to step into her mess and offer hope? Was grace real? Could forgiveness reach even those who feel completely unworthy?
Here’s something easy to miss: grace doesn’t always arrive with fanfare. Sometimes it looks like a friend who won’t give up on you, just quietly listening when everyone else walks away. Other times, it’s a stranger’s smile, a kind word, or just a simple moment of being seen. Those little acts of love become lifelines—a quiet reminder that brokenness isn’t the end of the story.
During this season, she realized that the walls built to keep out pain also kept out love. Healing, she discovered, takes vulnerability. It means admitting you need help and being willing to receive it. That can be terrifying for someone used to being strong. But as the old ways of coping failed, surrender started to seem less like defeat—and more like freedom.
The journey through brokenness is hard. It’s full of tears, regrets, and the slow process of letting go. But it’s also where real transformation starts. In the darkness, hope doesn’t show up as a quick fix—but as a gentle invitation to believe things can get better.
Looking back, it’s clear that rock bottom wasn’t the end. It was a turning point—the place where pride gave way to humility, and self-reliance turned into dependence on something bigger. If you’ve ever felt too broken to be loved, hear this: no one is beyond the reach of grace.

Chapter 3: Unexpected Encounters with Grace and Love.
Sometimes, the biggest changes in our lives sneak up on us in the most ordinary moments. You might expect some kind of grand spiritual awakening—with fireworks, maybe a dramatic sign from above. But honestly? It’s usually a lot quieter than that. Sometimes it’s just a conversation, a song you hear at the right time, or a simple act of kindness that cuts through all the pain and disappointment we’ve built up.
After a season of brokenness, life doesn’t magically become easy. The old struggles don’t just disappear, and those doubts? They tend to stick around, whispering in the background. But here’s the thing: something inside shifts. There’s a new openness—a readiness to see the world through different eyes. And it’s in that vulnerable space that moments of unexpected grace start to show up.
Picture this: one afternoon, you’re sitting alone in a busy coffee shop, not expecting anything out of the ordinary. But then, you find yourself drawn into a conversation with a total stranger. It starts off with the usual small talk—the weather, work, nothing special. But pretty soon, you’re talking about real things. The stranger shares stories about hope, about finding purpose even when life feels chaotic, about a love that never gives up. There’s just something about this person—a calm confidence, a peace that’s almost contagious.
Most people might brush off an encounter like that as just coincidence. But for her, it felt like a lifeline. Those words stuck with her, echoing long after she left. They stirred up questions, and maybe even a longing for something more. Could it really be that God uses everyday people to deliver extraordinary messages?
Over the next few weeks, moments like this kept popping up. A random song on the radio spoke right to her deepest fears. A friend invited her to church, and the message there seemed like it was written just for her. Even the simple beauty of a sunrise, the sound of rain, or the laughter of children became gentle reminders that life is about more than just getting by.
Now, these experiences didn’t magically erase her pain or answer every tough question. But they did spark hope. She began to realize that grace isn’t something you earn; it’s a gift you just receive. The idea of a God who pursues us, who loves us without conditions, started to make sense. For maybe the first time, faith felt less like a heavy burden and more like an open invitation.
During all this, one thing became really clear: healing almost never happens when you’re alone. It’s in community—real, messy, imperfect relationships—that transformation takes root. Friends who listened without judging, mentors who shared their own stories, and a faith community that welcomed every question played a huge part in her journey.
Of course, there were setbacks. Old habits don’t just disappear overnight, and the temptation to retreat, to protect yourself, is always there. But each time she stumbled, she found herself caught—not by her own strength, but by a love that refused to let go. Learning to trust, to really believe she was seen and loved, was slow and sometimes painful. Yet with every step, the grip of shame and fear got a little weaker.
And looking back now, it’s obvious those encounters with grace weren’t just random. They were pieces of a bigger story—a story about pursuit, about a God who never gives up on the lost or broken. If you’ve ever questioned whether you’re worthy of love, these moments offer a quiet assurance: grace finds us where we are, not where we think we should be.

Chapter 4: Embracing Faith and Discovering a New Identity
There comes a point in every journey when the old ways just... don’t fit anymore. Maybe you’ve felt it—that moment when the masks you once wore to protect yourself start to feel more like a burden than a shield. Suddenly, searching for meaning isn’t just a nice idea; it feels urgent, even necessary. For some, this is where faith steps in—not as a distant concept, but as a lifeline. Imagine a young woman, months into wrestling with her doubts and tough questions. She finds herself at a crossroads. There’s this quiet invitation—trust, believe in a love that’s been chasing her, even in her darkest moments. It’s scary, sure. But at the same time, it’s oddly compelling. Here’s the thing: she doesn’t have all the answers. In fact, she’s not even sure she knows the right questions. But she’s willing to take even the smallest step toward something new. Choosing faith isn’t about big, dramatic moments. Sometimes, it’s a quiet surrender—a whispered prayer in the middle of the night. And in that stillness, something shifts. The weight of shame, the regret she’s been carrying? It starts to lift. In its place, a peace settles in—a peace that doesn’t really make sense, but feels real all the same. Suddenly, her identity isn’t tied to past mistakes or what others think. It’s rooted in being loved—deeply, unconditionally—by the One who made her. A lot of people think faith is all about rules or keeping score. But honestly, it’s much more personal than that. It’s about relationship—a daily, ongoing conversation with a God who knows you, who actually cares about what you’re going through. For her, this meant learning to listen. Trusting that she’s not alone in the mess. Letting go of the need to control everything, and discovering a freedom she never thought possible—the kind that comes from being known and accepted, just as she is. As faith started to grow, new habits took root. Where she once criticized herself or compared her life to others, gratitude and compassion began to take over. The urge to prove she was worthy faded, replaced by a quiet confidence—grounded in the simple truth that she’s loved. Of course, transformation didn’t happen overnight. There were still days filled with doubt, moments when fear crept in. But each day brought new opportunities—a chance to choose trust over anxiety, hope over despair. And she didn’t do it alone. Community made a world of difference. Being surrounded by others on the same road gave her encouragement and accountability. Sharing stories of struggle and redemption reminded her—no one has to walk this path alone. In these relationships, faith became real. Not just an idea, but something lived out, day by day. There were tough moments, too. Not everyone understood the changes happening inside her. Some relationships became strained. But even then, she sensed a deep belonging—being part of something bigger than herself. Looking back, it’s clear: embracing faith wasn’t the finish line. It was just the start of a brand new chapter. She began to discover a different identity—one that doesn’t depend on performance or approval, but on the steady, unchanging love of God. So if you’ve ever wondered whether real change is possible, here’s some hope for you: transformation begins with one small step of trust.

Chapter 5: Learning to Live with Purpose and Hope
So, after the whirlwind of transformation, when the dust finally settles, you might find yourself asking—what now? It’s one thing to experience healing and grace. But living out that new reality, day in and day out? Well, that’s a whole different story.
See, faith isn’t just a one-time moment. It’s really about making the choice, every single day, to walk forward with hope and a sense of purpose.
If you’ve spent years searching for meaning, finally discovering your purpose can feel both thrilling and, honestly, a little scary. Suddenly, there’s this urge to make an impact—to use all those hard-earned lessons, even the painful ones, to help someone else. And you begin to realize, your story of brokenness and redemption isn’t just yours to keep. It’s meant to be shared.
Take the story of a young woman who, after choosing faith, found herself drawn to serve others. Maybe she volunteered at a local shelter. Or spent time mentoring younger students. Sometimes, she’d just listen when a friend needed it most. Through these simple acts, she discovered something powerful—purpose often shows up in the way we love others. Even the smallest gestures of kindness became expressions of the grace she’d experienced herself.
Here’s something to remember—most people underestimate the power of simple faithfulness. We tend to think living with purpose requires big, dramatic gestures or a spotlight. But, in reality, it’s usually much quieter. It’s about showing up. Choosing compassion instead of indifference. Offering hope to someone who feels invisible. Every small act of love is a way of joining a bigger story.
Of course, living with purpose isn’t always easy. There’ll be days when doubts sneak back in, or old fears try to pull you off course. It’s tempting to slip back into familiar patterns. But in those moments, remembering how you were once found and loved gives you strength to keep moving forward. Hope isn’t the absence of struggle—it’s the courage to believe that redemption is possible, even when things still hurt.
Over time, your journey of transformation can actually inspire others. When you’re honest about both your struggles and your victories, you create a safe space for people to open up about their own stories. And it’s in sharing these real-life moments that the idea of grace becomes something you can actually feel—offering hope to anyone who’s still searching.
Looking back, maybe you realize the journey never really ends. There are still questions, still days full of uncertainty. But there’s also a deep, steady peace—a quiet confidence that, no matter what happens, love is never going to let go.
So if you’ve ever wondered whether your story matters, take this to heart—every life, no matter how broken, can become a living testimony of hope.

Chapter 6: The Ongoing Struggle with Doubt and Fear
You know, even after that first wave of hope, life has a funny way of circling back to those old questions.
Doubt doesn’t just vanish the moment faith takes root. Instead, it kind of sneaks back in—quieter, softer, almost like a shadow that just lingers at the edge of your happiness.
Honestly, this is one of the most vulnerable parts of the journey: realizing that faith and fear can show up at the exact same time.
There are mornings when everything feels heavy again. Out of nowhere, that old ache comes back. Maybe it’s something small—a harsh word from a coworker, a letdown at home, or just the weight of not knowing what’s next.
Suddenly, all those questions start swirling. “Am I really loved? Is God still here? What if I’m just not enough?”
The thing is, these doubts don’t always shout. Sometimes, they just slip in quietly, hidden behind tiredness or feeling restless for no clear reason.
Let me tell you about a moment that really brings this to life.
One night, after an especially tough day, a woman sat alone in her car, just staring at the dashboard lights. The silence around her felt almost too much. She remembered the promises she’d held onto, those moments of peace she’d felt before, but now... they seemed so far away.
Tears came, uninvited. And right there, in that quiet, she whispered a prayer—not fancy or confident, just honest. “Are you still with me?”
Most of us don’t really talk about these moments, do we? There’s this unspoken pressure to look strong, to act like having faith means you never struggle. But here’s the truth—everyone faces seasons of doubt.
What really matters isn’t having all the answers. It’s being willing to bring your questions out into the open. Over time, this woman discovered something powerful: God’s love didn’t depend on her certainty. Even in the middle of her fear, she wasn’t alone.
Community became a lifeline. Just having friends who listened without judging, who shared their own stories of wrestling with doubt, made all the difference. In those safe spaces, she could be honest about her struggles without worrying about being rejected. Sometimes, just being seen and heard is enough to make the load feel lighter.
Looking back, it’s easier to see how those seasons of doubt actually deepened her faith. They stripped away the illusion of control and helped her lean on something bigger than herself.
So, if you’ve ever felt ashamed of your questions, let this be a gentle reminder: doubt isn’t a sign of failure. It’s actually an invitation—to trust more deeply.

Chapter 7: Forgiveness—Letting Go and Moving Forward.
Forgiveness. It’s one of those words that sounds so simple—until you’re the one who has to actually do it. Letting go of past hurts? That’s easy to talk about, but when the pain runs deep, it’s a whole different story. If you’ve ever tried to forgive someone who really hurt you, you know it’s not a straight line. Sometimes, it feels like one step forward, two steps back.
Picture this: There was a time when memories of betrayal and disappointment kept replaying in her mind, like a song she just couldn’t turn off. Every time, the pain felt just as raw as the first. And honestly, the idea of forgiving the people who caused it? That seemed impossible. She’d ask herself, “Why should I let go? Shouldn’t they know how much they hurt me?” In a way, holding on to that anger felt right—almost protective.
But you know what? Over time, something shifted. She realized that clutching that resentment was really just building her own prison. The bitterness she thought would protect her, it only made the wounds deeper. Then, one quiet afternoon in the park, while journaling, she ended up writing a letter she never planned to send. She poured out everything—the hurt, the anger, and finally, the hope to be free. That simple act of writing it down? It was a turning point. It didn’t erase what happened, but it loosened the grip of bitterness.
Here’s something to pay attention to: Forgiveness isn’t really about the other person. It’s about giving yourself the chance to be free. For her, it meant making a choice—sometimes every single day—to let go of that old story of pain, and start embracing a new story, one filled with grace.
Of course, there were days when the old anger came rushing back, especially when fresh wounds opened up old scars. But each time, she remembered the forgiveness she’d received—the grace that met her right in her own brokenness. And slowly, she learned to extend that same grace to others.
Forgiveness doesn’t mean pretending the pain never happened, or just forgetting. It’s about choosing to move forward, refusing to let the past write the rest of your story. In the end, forgiveness is really an act of courage—a way to reclaim hope, and open the door to healing.
So if you’re struggling to let go, consider this a gentle invitation: forgiveness isn’t just a single moment—it’s a journey. And along that path, real freedom is possible.

Chapter 8: The Surprising Power of Surrender
There’s a kind of freedom that shows up only when you finally stop trying to control every little thing.
For years, surrender almost felt like a sign of weakness to me—like it was something you did when you just couldn’t handle life on your own.
But as time went on, I started to realize: surrender isn’t about giving up. It’s about letting go of that exhausting illusion that you’re in charge of everything.
Life, as you know, has this funny way of reminding us just how little we can actually predict or manage.
Maybe you’ve seen it too—plans unraveling, relationships shifting, the future staying stubbornly out of focus.
Let me tell you about one woman’s turning point, during a season when everything felt up in the air. She’d been counting on a new job, and just like that, it vanished.
Suddenly, she was left anxious, untethered. The old urge to fix things, to force a solution, kicked in hard.
But this time... something was different.
Instead of scrambling for answers, she just sat quietly—hands open in her lap.
She remembered words from an old prayer: “Not my will, but yours.”
It wasn’t some dramatic, movie-worthy moment. There were no lightning bolts, no big revelations.
Just a gentle sense of release—a willingness to trust that she didn’t have to have everything figured out.
Most of us resist surrender because it feels a lot like losing, doesn’t it?
But in that quiet moment, it became clear: surrender was actually an act of trust—a way of admitting we’re not alone in all this.
The anxiety that had been gripping her started to loosen. In its place was a surprising sense of peace.
Over the next few weeks, new opportunities showed up.
Not the ones she would’ve chosen for herself, but, looking back, exactly what she needed.
It became obvious: letting go actually made room for something better.
Surrender doesn’t mean giving up or checking out.
It’s about showing up, doing what you can, and then letting the rest fall into hands far more capable than your own.
So if you’ve ever felt worn out from trying to control it all, here’s a gentle reminder: sometimes, your greatest strength is found in letting go.

Let’s talk about something that’s both incredibly rewarding and, honestly, pretty tough— Loving Others—The Challenge and the Gift.
It’s one thing to talk about love like it’s this beautiful, lofty idea. But living it out? Especially when life gets messy, or people aren’t exactly easy to love? That’s where things get real.
Think about it—sometimes, loving others comes naturally. Maybe your friends are being thoughtful, your family’s got your back, and everything just feels smooth. But, more often than not, love takes real effort.
It means listening when you’d rather jump in and speak your mind. Forgiving, even when holding onto that grudge feels easier. Or showing up, again and again, when walking away would be the simpler choice.
There’s this one memory that really stands out—a tense moment with a coworker who seemed determined to misunderstand her. You know that feeling, right? The urge to get sarcastic or just check out completely? But instead, she remembered all those times others had been patient and kind with her.
So, she took a deep breath and chose to listen instead of defend. The conversation didn’t magically fix itself, but something shifted. The walls between them started to crumble, and in their place, a little spark of respect appeared.
Here’s something easy to overlook: the true power of small acts of love. A smile. An encouraging word. Just giving someone the benefit of the doubt. These little things? They’re the building blocks of real connection.
Over time, it became clear—love isn’t just a feeling. It’s a choice you make, over and over. It’s deciding to show up, to be vulnerable, and to believe every person is worthy of kindness.
But loving others isn’t about being a doormat, either. Sometimes, it means setting boundaries—learning to say no when you need to, and realizing that taking care of yourself isn’t selfish at all. It’s a balancing act, and it takes both wisdom and grace.
Looking back, the moments of the greatest growth were usually the ones that asked for the most love. And if you’ve ever struggled to love well, here’s a little hope for you: love isn’t about getting it perfect. It’s about showing up, time and time again, with an open heart.

Chapter 10: Living in the Reality of Being Pursued.
Have you ever felt like something—someone—was reaching for you, even in the smallest moments of your day? As this journey unfolded, that sense of being pursued started to become real. Not just as a memory or a comforting idea, but as something alive and present, every single day.
It’s the kind of love that doesn’t just sit back and wait. It’s active, ongoing, relentless. God’s love became more than just a warm thought—it became a reality she could feel and live out. There were days when it was obvious—a word of encouragement at just the right time, a surprise that met a need, or a deep peace that showed up in the middle of chaos.
But honestly? Most of the time, that pursuit was subtle. It was the sunrise painting hope across the sky. The sound of a friend’s laughter that broke through the weight of a tough day. Or maybe it was just a quiet confidence that, no matter what happened, she wasn’t alone.
One evening, as she walked through her neighborhood, she noticed the way the sunlight streamed through the trees. It was such a small thing—easy to miss. But right then, it felt like a gentle reminder: love is always reaching out. It’s inviting us to notice, to receive, and to respond.
Most of us hurry through life. We miss those little signs that we’re being pursued. But as she learned to slow down and pay attention, those signs became impossible to ignore. They were right there in the everyday moments—the ordinary stuff that shapes our lives.
Living in the reality of being pursued changed everything. Suddenly, there was a deep sense of security—a confidence that she was wanted, chosen, and cherished. And with that came a new responsibility: to share this love, to become someone who pursues hope for others in a world that so often feels lost.
Looking back, it’s clear—the story was never just about her searching for God. It was about God searching for her, every step of the way. If you’ve ever wondered whether you’re worth pursuing, let this chapter be your quiet assurance: you are seen, you are wanted, and you are loved—exactly where you are, right now.
Conclusion: Living the Story—An Invitation to Trust and Hope
If you’ve been following along on this journey, you probably know by now—faith isn’t a neat, straight path. It winds, it twists, and it’s full of questions, setbacks, and those surprising moments of grace. The story of being pursued and found? It’s not just for one person. It’s an open invitation—for all of us.
Here are a few gentle reminders to tuck into your heart as you go:
Faith really grows in the soil of honest questions and real struggles. Grace? It finds us right in the middle of our mess, not when we’ve got everything together. Forgiveness is a gift you get to give yourself, not only the people who’ve hurt you. Surrender isn’t weakness—it’s the doorway to peace and new possibilities. And love? It’s a choice we make each day, often in small, unseen moments.
You don’t have to have it all figured out. You don’t have to be perfect, or even completely sure, to take the next step. This story of being pursued by love—it’s always unfolding. There’s always more to discover, more to receive, and more to share. If you’re doubting, struggling, or feeling invisible, please know—you are not alone. The journey is long, but you are being carried, even when you can’t see it.
So, let this story be a gentle nudge. A reminder that your questions are welcome, your pain is seen, and your hope truly matters. Take your next step, no matter how small. Trust that love is reaching for you, right now—in the middle of your ordinary, imperfect life. And as you keep going, may you find the courage to live your own story of being pursued, found, and loved—one day at a time.
